text:
Maya: Heads-up — a strategic customer asked for a mobile-optimized low‑latency variant of our gpt-open-1 catalog model. Requirement: 512-token chat, 95th pct API-to-client latency <120ms. They want hosted + dedicated first, private later. Can eng-runtime scope the work (kernel selection, quant profiles, KV prefetch/eviction) and produce an RFC? /cc @Dan @Simon
Dan: Quick clarifying q — is the 120ms SLO end-to-end (API→client) or server-side generation only? We need that to set realistic infra targets.
Maya: API→client 95th including network. Customer is NA mobile heavy. Product wants a graceful fallback (higher-latency but still acceptable) if the optimized path can't serve.
Simon: +1. For mobile we should target 4/8-bit quant profiles and a fused-attn kernel path. We'll need a variant in the kernel catalog with KV-optimized memory layout. Also need to decide prefetch: warm prefix prefetch vs on-demand.
Raj: Acceptance criteria proposal (draft):
- 95th pct API→client <120ms for 512-token interactions under target load (50 qps tenant).
- 99th pct API→client <250ms.
- p50 server generation <30ms.
- Per-request GPU memory overhead <= 1.2GB additional vs baseline.
- No correctness regressions on existing eval suite (<=1% quality delta on top customer prompts).
Dan: Good start. We should also include rollout gates: perf regression <2% on A/B traffic, canary at 1%→10%→50% with automatic rollback.
Maya: Can we get an RFC outline that covers: kernel selection matrix (hw × model × sequence length), quant profiles and fallback ordering, KV prefetch & eviction policy, rollout plan with canary thresholds, required metrics/alerts, and privacy/security checklist for Private?
Raj: I'll draft. Scope question: do we include Private (VPC/on‑prem) in the initial launch? Customer asked for Private as requirement but Product suggested delaying until we stabilize hosted+dedi.
Dan: Recommend hosted + dedicated in phase 1, Private in phase 2. Private has extra rollout tasks (KMS integration, packaging).
Simon: Edge cases we need in RFC tests:
- Cold starts where client sends long initial context (>2048) that triggers KV chaining.
- Tokenization variance causing cache miss storms across sessions.
- Partial KV hits when clients rotate session keys.
- Kernel-switch overhead when a session moves between quant variants.
We should add synthetic workloads that simulate mobile networking jitter.
Raj: Draft config snippet for RFC (example):
```
{"kernel_policy": "mobile_opt_v1",
 "quant_profiles": ["q4_0","q8_1","fp16"],
 "prefetch": {"strategy": "warm_prefix", "warm_prefix_len": 48, "max_prefetch_bytes": 64_000_000},
 "eviction": {"policy": "lru_session", "min_reserve_mb": 256},
 "rollout": {"canary_steps": [1,10,50], "rollback_on": ["latency_p95_increase>2%","error_rate_increase>0.5%"]}
}
```
Maya: Timeline ask from Product: RFC by next Tue, perf microbench infra by EOW, first canary in ~2 weeks if perf looks good. Customers want a demo for their SREs in 3 weeks.
Dan: I'll assign reviewers: Simon (ML infra), Lee (perf), Olga (security/compliance). Also tag metric owners for latency/error_rate/apdex and a rollout owner.
Lee: Perf note — log kernel_variant and kernel_switch_count per session. Track distribution of switch_count; target median 0 and 95th <=1 for steady traffic. Also measure end-to-end client variance to correlate network vs server tail.
Olga: Security items — Private must have KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. Add model access audit events and disallow model weight dump in debug logs. Rate-limits default should prevent noisy-tenant problems.
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/1768451234-mobile-opt-rfc (draft).
Raj: Acknowledged. I'll attach microbench harness (mobile-net jitter profiles + synthetic tokenization) and a short acceptance-run checklist to the RFC.
Maya: Thanks — once RFC lands we'll triage follow-ups (test matrices, infra cost estimate, perf owners).
Dan: Assigned tasks in RFC. I'll post an initial draft by EOD tomorrow for quick feedback.
